verses.text: Josiah celebrated Passover to the LORD in Jerusalem. They slaughtered the Passover animals on the fourteenth day of the first month.
He assigned the priests their duties and encouraged them as they served in the LORD’s house.

He told the Levites, who taught all Israel and were set apart for the LORD, “Put the holy ark in the house built by Solomon son of David, king of Israel. You won’t have to carry it on your shoulders anymore. Now serve the LORD your God and his people Israel.
Get ready in teams by your ancestral families, following the written instructions of King David of Israel and his son Solomon.
Stand in the holy place according to the family groups of your fellow Israelites. Assign part of a Levite family to each group.
Slaughter the Passover lambs, set yourselves apart, and make preparations for your fellow Israelites so they can follow the LORD’s word given through Moses.”
From his own flocks, Josiah gave everyone there thirty thousand lambs and young goats for the Passover offerings, along with three thousand bulls. All of it came from the king’s own property.

His officials gave willingly to the people, priests, and Levites. Hilkiah, Zechariah, and Jehiel, who were in charge of God’s house, gave the priests twenty-six hundred sheep and goats and three hundred cattle for the Passover offerings.

Conaniah and his brothers Shemaiah and Nethanel, along with Hashabiah, Jeiel, and Jozabad, the Levite leaders, gave the Levites five thousand sheep and goats and five hundred cattle for the Passover offerings.
Everything was ready for worship. The priests took their places and the Levites got into their teams, just as the king had commanded.
They slaughtered the Passover lambs. The priests took the blood from the Levites and sprinkled it, and the Levites skinned the animals.
They set aside the burnt offerings to hand out to the people by family group, so the families could offer them to the LORD, as written in the book of Moses. They did the same with the cattle.
They roasted the Passover animals over a fire as required. They boiled the holy offerings in pots, cauldrons, and pans, then rushed the food out to all the people.
After that the Levites made food for themselves and for the priests descended from Aaron, who were busy offering the burnt offerings and the fat until night.

The singers descended from Asaph stayed at their posts as David, Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun, the king’s seer, had directed. Gatekeepers were at every gate. They could stay on duty because their fellow Levites prepared food for them.
So that day everything for the LORD’s service was ready. They celebrated Passover and offered burnt offerings on the LORD’s altar as King Josiah had commanded.
The Israelites who were there celebrated Passover at that time and kept the Festival of Unleavened Bread for seven days.

Israel hadn’t seen a Passover like it since the days of the prophet Samuel. None of Israel’s kings had celebrated one like Josiah did with the priests and Levites, everyone there from Judah and Israel, and the people of Jerusalem.
They celebrated this Passover in Josiah’s eighteenth year as king.
After all this, once Josiah had put the temple in order, King Neco of Egypt marched to fight at Carchemish by the Euphrates. Josiah went out to face him.

Neco sent messengers to say, “What quarrel do I have with you, king of Judah? I didn’t come to fight you today. I’m going against the house I’m at war with. God told me to hurry. God is with me, so watch out or he’ll destroy you.”
Josiah refused to back off. He disguised himself to fight Neco and ignored what Neco had said from God’s own mouth. He went to fight in the valley of Megiddo.
The archers shot King Josiah. He told his servants, “Get me out of here! I’m badly wounded!”
His servants lifted him out of his chariot, put him in his second chariot, and took him to Jerusalem. He died and was buried in the tombs of his ancestors. All Judah and Jerusalem mourned for him.

Jeremiah sang a lament for Josiah. To this day, singers, both men and women, remember Josiah in their songs of mourning. Israel made it an established custom, and the songs are written in the collection of laments.
The rest of what Josiah did, including the good he did in keeping with the LORD’s written law,
along with his other acts from first to last, is recorded in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.
